## Run

In the LTEE project, Snakemake is in the `pipeline` environment: put
`pixi run -e pipeline` in front of each command (or use the task:
`pixi run run-snakemake`).

| What you want | Command |
|------------|------------------------|
| Dry run: what would run, and why | `snakemake -n` (summary only: `-n --quiet`; show the commands: `-n -p`) |
| Make everything in `rule all`, with 4 cores | `snakemake -c 4` |
| Make one file | `snakemake -c 4 results/bam/SRR2584863.aligned.sorted.bam.bai` |
| Change a setting for one run | `snakemake -c 4 --config bwa_extra=""` |
| Draw the job graph | `snakemake --dag dot TARGET > results/dag.dot`, then `dot -Tsvg results/dag.dot -o results/dag.svg` |
| Draw the rule graph | `snakemake --rulegraph > results/rulegraph.dot`, then `dot -Tsvg ...` |
| Format the Snakefile / check the format | `snakefmt workflow/Snakefile` / `snakefmt --check workflow/Snakefile` |
| Check for common mistakes | `snakemake --lint` |
| Run on a cluster with a profile | `snakemake --profile profiles/karakoram` |

See [lesson 09, sections 2, 5 and 12](../pages/09-snakemake.qmd#a-toy-workflow-first).

## A rule

```{.python}
rule bwa_mem:
    input:
        genome=GENOME,
        r1=lambda wc: SAMPLES[wc.sample]["fastq_1"],   # an input function
        r2=lambda wc: SAMPLES[wc.sample]["fastq_2"],
    output:
        temp("results/sam/{sample}.aligned.sam"),     # {sample} is a wildcard
    log:
        "results/logs/bwa_mem/{sample}.log",
    threads: 4
    params:
        extra=config["bwa_extra"],
    shell:
        "bwa mem -t {threads} {params.extra} {input.genome} {input.r1} {input.r2} > {output} 2> {log}"
```

## Building blocks

| Write | What it does |
|------------|------------------------|
| `configfile: "config/config.yaml"`, then `config["min_depth"]` | settings in YAML, out of the code |
| `{sample}` in `output:` | a wildcard, filled in from the file you ask for |
| `expand("results/vcf/{sample}_final_variants.vcf", sample=SAMPLES)` | a list of files, one per sample |
| `rule all:` with `default_target: True` | the files a plain `snakemake` makes |
| `temp("FILE")` | delete the file once no rule needs it |
| `log:` | a file for the tool's messages |
| `threads: 4` and `{threads}` | how many cores the rule may use |
| `rules.bwa_index.output` | the output of another rule |
| `multiext(GENOME, ".amb", ".bwt")` | one name with several endings |
| `wildcard_constraints:` | what a wildcard may match |

See [sections 3 to 9](../pages/09-snakemake.qmd#settings-first-the-config-file).

## When does a job rerun?

When its output is missing, or older than an input (**mtime**), or when the
rule's **code**, **params**, set of **input** files or **software
environment** changed since the output was made. Ask with `snakemake -n`: it
prints the reason for each job. See [rerun triggers](../pages/09-snakemake.qmd#rerun-triggers).

## Official cheat sheets and references

Snakemake has no official cheat sheet. The closest official references:

- Snakemake, *Command line interface* (every option): <https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/en/stable/executing/cli.html>
- Snakemake, *Snakefiles and Rules* (every rule keyword): <https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/en/stable/snakefiles/rules.html>
- Snakemake, *Basics: an example workflow* (the official tutorial): <https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tutorial/basics.html>
- The Snakemake workflow template: <https://github.com/snakemake-workflows/snakemake-workflow-template>
